name: Mama
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog cites only classification works (Maddieson & Williamson 1975; Green 2022); no grammar/phonology of Mama (Kantana) found on OLAC-mirror, archive.org, or OpenLibrary.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalogue, resources in and about the Mama language [mma] (Wayback 2026-05-19)
sources.note: Only Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List entries; no archived recordings, wordlists or descriptions.

sources.citation: Rueck, Mike & Zachariah Yoder. 2011. ISO 639-3 change request 2011-171 and Request for New Language Code Element (Kantana, proposed jkt). SIL International.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic only (Kanam/Alkaleri Kantana, 2,000-3,000 speakers, closest to Bada or Duguri). Identity statement: 'Gerhardt includes data from a "Kantana" in his 1988 paper... but this is actually from Mama [mma], whose alternate name is Kantana'; M&W 1975 p. 135 mention Kantana as origin of the Mama people. Lists all known sources: Blench 2006, Gerhardt 1988, M&W 1975, Shimizu 1983.

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1988. A note on verbal extensions in Jarawan Bantu. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 3-8.
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Verbal extensions in Kantana' pp. 7-8 (page images checked): Tables 6-8 give tone-marked verb pairs (perfective -na / V-lengthening + final -a; intensive ?+copy vowel); 'CVC stem... is by far the most frequent shape of words in Kantana'. No word on stress, accent or tone anywhere in the paper (the scanned string 'Heavy stress' p. 6 is a misprint for 'Heavy stems' in the Jaar section).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2026. The Jarawan Bantu languages in Nigeria; what is new research telling us? Slides, Jos Linguistic Circle, 15 July 2026 (Academia.edu page text via Wayback)
sources.note: Mama appears only as a branch in the classification tree (Kantana inside Jarawa); tone remarks are given for Labir and Gura only; nothing on Mama.

sources.citation: Ethnologue (free edition) page for Mama [mma] (Wayback 2025-08-12)
sources.note: Endangered, <10K users, Niger-Congo; no references or linguistic content.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Uebersee 97. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288
sources.note: p. 19 table lists Jarawan languages 'Jar, Mbula-Bwazza, Mama'; p. 24 tone table 'Jarawan -- No analysis'; 'Some families, such as Jarawan, lack a single reliable synchronic description of tone.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2020. Harmony and disharmony in Mbat (Jarawan Bantu) verbs. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 6: 43-72.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Concerns Mbat (bada1258), not Mama; H/M/L surface tones for Mbat; no stress statement; Mama not mentioned.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 / 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. III / ed. IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Entry 305/306 'Mama; 2.B Kwarra, Kantana; Nasarawa State, Akwanga LGA; 7,891 (1922 Temple), 6,155 (1934 Ames), 20,000 (1973 SIL)'; Source(s) and Refs fields empty. Index: 'Kantana - dialect of Bada: see the Jar cluster'; 'Kantana = Mama'; 'Kwarra = Mama'. No phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Jarawan Bantu: new data and its relation to Bantu. Circulation draft, Cambridge, 12 Jan 2006, 20 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Tree (p. 2) lists Mama and Kantana as separate nodes; comparative wordlist pp. 3-15 carries a near-empty 'Mama' column (BCCW / Ibadan questionnaire data); 'Gerhardt (1982 [sic, =1988]) provides data on verbal extensions in Mama and Kantana'. No phonological remarks.

sources.citation: Temple, O. (comp.) & C. L. Temple (ed.). 1922. Notes on the tribes, provinces, emirates and states of the Northern Provinces of Nigeria, 2nd ed. Lagos: CMS Bookshop.
sources.note: Entry 'MAMA' pp. 267-268: ethnography only (7,891 people, four clans, Lafia Division of Nassarawa Province, 'apparent resemblance to the Bantu stock', clans' dialects mutually hard to understand, duodecimal counting). No linguistic data.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mama1272 (Mama; alt. names Kantana, Kwarra)
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all: only Green 2022 and Maddieson & Williamson 1975 (both cited for subclassification) and Ethnologue 2025; n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Mama language' and 'Jarawan languages' (raw wikitext)
sources.note: Mama page is a stub citing only Ethnologue and ISO CR 2011-171. Jarawan page: Gerhardt 1988 is the only work treating Kantana morphology; Green's work (2018-) is on Mbat and Duguri; no Mama phonology cited.
